props.gloss_en: the mishna: which is not so of blood -- blood [of offerings] is not subject to me'ila
Ulla: the verse says 'to you' (Lev 17:11) -- it shall be yours
the school of R' Yishmael: 'to atone' -- I gave it for atonement, and not for me'ila
R' Yochanan: the verse says 'it' -- it is before atonement as after atonement: as after atonement it has no me'ila, so before atonement it has no me'ila
there is nothing whose mitzva has been done and which is [still] subject to me'ila
the removal of the ashes: its mitzva is done and it is subject to me'ila, as written 'and he shall put it beside the altar' (Lev 6:3)
and any two verses that come as one do not teach
the Rabbis: 'and he shall leave them there' (Lev 16:23) teaches that [the garments] require interment
R' Dosa: [it teaches only] that he may not use them on another Yom Kippur
three verses ['to you', 'to atone', 'it'] are stated of blood
and one to exclude it from impurity
but from piggul no verse is needed
the mishna (Zevachim 43a): anything that has permitters, whether for man or for the altar, one is liable for it on account of piggul
and blood itself is a permitter
